A user praised the 2FA-via-email use case. They had built a browser automation workflow needing 2FA and used Zapier to watch an inbox, extract the code and send it back to their API, which was 'a bit slow.'
In reply to the 2FA use case, a commenter asked why not use Mailinator, saying it specializes in exactly this and offers an API to grab links: 'That's what I use.'

Loading www.agentmail.to produced 'Application error: a client-side exception has occurred.' The console showed 'Failed to create WebGL context: WebGL is currently disabled' and a rejected cookie. The user asked why an email website needs WebGL and suspected it was vibe-coded.
Design gripe: on agentmail.to/enterprise, the cutesy ASCII art is rendered in a proportional rather than monospace font, 'so it looks terrible.'

A user said scrolling the AgentMail site produced lag they had 'genuinely never witnessed in any website,' with images loading 10% at a time. They couldn't view it on a 16GB computer. Switching the code example from Python to curl also lagged noticeably.

An O365 GCC shop said it has many enterprise AI use cases that would benefit from being email native. They appreciated that the enterprise options include Bring Your Own Cloud, which 'makes things much easier for us.' They would like integrations with n8n and Glean.
Several commenters questioned differentiation: 'Looks like SES + api access, isn't Amazon offering that already?' Another said API-based scripted email access isn't new.
A skeptic claimed they could build to parity in a weekend on Cloudflare without the pricing limitations, likely within CF's free tier.
Pricing suggestion: keep the volume limits but offer 10x the number of inboxes per plan. That would suit users running hundreds of agents that each send limited email.

Concern that the service will attract abusers using it to sign up for services or spam, getting the domain blacklisted: 'an infinite whack-a-mole.' Another user asked what prevents prompt injection if an agent's address is known.
A business owner said their customer service staff are told not to respond to apparent bots, because all the 'agent' based email they receive is scams.
Positive: a user wants to use it to help customers handle email responses, saying 'Gmail sucks for this.' They asked about expanding to payments or phone numbers.

Alternative: default Gmail offers free webhooks for any changes via Gmail pubsub. The user relies on it for credit card purchase alerts parsed with regex: 'Super fast low latency very satisfying. Pubsub scales well and free.'
'Pricing is a bit steep for a startup currently looking to prove the market.' $100/month is 'a deep hole' before an MVP is proven. The user asked for 1 free inbox or $20/mo for 5 inboxes.
A user wanted to try AgentMail for an internal agent but found it still on a waitlist, and the 'contact us' and 'contact sales' buttons weren't clickable.
Praise for the dashboard's popovers showing SDK examples: 'a brilliant UI idea (executed with great polish)' and the first time this user had seen it.
'Onboarding/signup started off great, but then you just drop in with no clarity on what to do next. A lot of actions possible and I'm unsure what to do first.'

A user considering building something similar said they might just use AgentMail ('looks great!'). But they already use Postmark, which released an open-source MCP server, and asked why they would switch.

'Many vendors might look like they have similar capabilities on a powerpoint, but when you look one level deeper, they really don't.' Example: webhook notifications at 1-minute intervals bundling many emails vs instant, single-email notifications.
Responding to claims of 'sky high' rate limits, a skeptic said: 'Let me know how long that'll last. The low limits of other providers are there for a reason. That reason's called spam.'
